A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Memory-V2V. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures are readable and can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original novel-view synthesis and long-video editing experiments, component ablations, computational measurements and appendix context-encoder experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds ground-truth reconstruction results, additional baseline evaluations and qualitative editing demonstrations.

M1.justification: The cached VAE memory, VideoFOV/DINOv2 retrieval, dynamic tokenization, adaptive merging, training loss, RoPE assignments and camera conditioning remain unchanged. The added demonstrations do not document a modification to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix H and Fig. 19 add an interleaved editing scenario: reveal a region through camera motion, insert a moon, then revisit it through subsequent camera edits. The two principal tasks and training domains remain unchanged; the additional synchronized multi-camera validation primarily expands the evaluation protocol within existing coverage.

E2.justification: v3 materially broadens the evaluated alternatives by adding FlowEdit and DynVFX to the long-video comparison in Table 3 and Fig. 5, plus Runway Aleph with two conditioning variants in Appendix G. Existing baselines are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a ground-truth evaluation on 50 MultiCamVideo validation scenes with 10 synchronized views, randomly selected target and conditioning views, frame-wise PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS, and Top-1/Top-3 retrieval settings. Appendix G adds segment-wise Aleph testing with first- versus last-frame conditioning. The original benchmark protocols and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The original component, token-reduction and context-encoder ablations are retained. v3 adds focused analyses of memory quantity versus reconstruction fidelity, Aleph conditioning choices, and inserted-object persistence under revisited viewpoints in Table 5 and Figs. 16, 18 and 19.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains identical plus/minus summaries. Neither the added comparisons nor the new reconstruction evaluation introduces reported repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results remain unchanged, but v3 adds substantial new results in Tables 3 and 5 and qualitative demonstrations. Table 5 reports Top-3 PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS of 18.05/0.4767/0.2973. New Table 3 rows change several leaders: FlowEdit scores 0.8612/0.8943 on DINO-F/CLIP-F versus Memory-V2V's retained 0.8019/0.8741; DynVFX scores 0.5179 on aesthetic quality versus 0.4950.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, flow-matching derivation, retrieval equations and positional-conditioning formulation are unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 are reformatted without changing their mathematical operations; no new theorem, proof or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same substantive claims about memory as structured constraints, task-aware retrieval, efficient compression and improved cross-turn consistency. The added evidence does not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly qualifies DINO/CLIP similarity by edit success. The appendices interpret reconstruction results as evidence of 3D fidelity, discuss Aleph's conditioning trade-off, acknowledge that full task unification remains future work, and attribute specific artifacts to the base model or synthetic training segments. Existing multi-shot limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly mentions sharpness-based filtering, without specifying its criterion or threshold; this establishes additional disclosure, not a changed training procedure. Appendix G documents Aleph's five-second segment limit and conditioning choices. Existing hardware, training budgets and detailed implementation descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds FlowEdit and DynVFX references and discusses their relationship to the proposed approach, alongside the new Aleph comparison. The related-work taxonomy and central novelty positioning remain unchanged; most other citation edits are renumbering or bibliographic corrections.

P1.justification: Rewriting is concentrated in Section 4.3, the appendix roadmap and added appendix discussions. Author information, acknowledgements and running headers are updated. Most original prose and section ordering remain intact despite appendix renumbering.

P2.justification: Fig. 5 and Table 3 gain baseline rows; Table 5 and Figs. 16, 18 and 19 are added. Existing displays are relocated or renumbered, several qualitative panels use clearer, unblurred images, and Algorithms 1–2 receive different formatting. The overall visual organization remains recognizable.

improvement.justification: The ground-truth reconstruction evaluation and additional baselines strengthen empirical support, while metric qualifications and specific failure discussions improve transparency. These gains are limited by sparse details about the new evaluation's memory inputs and the retained blanket outperformance statement, which the expanded Table 3 does not support across all metrics. Overall, v3 provides a modest net improvement in validation and explanation.
